text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS
- Fourteen and 15-year-old minors who commit serious crimes could be sent to detention centre for up to two years.
- Economy Minister Rodrigo Rato launches austerity plan to cut costs of civil servants which includes limiting time of their official telephone calls.
EL MUNDO
- Ten thousand trade unionists will picket in general strike on December 11 in order to call two million public sector workers to protest against government's wage freeze.
- Real Madrid football player Pedja Mijatovic visits son in hospital.
DIARIO 16
- Former Secretary of State Rafael Vera breaks two years of silence and condemns use of dirty war against Basque separatist group ETA to topple former Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez.
ABC
- Defence Minister Eduardo Serra is to present plan on Tuesday for a professional army of 130,000 soldiers by 2003.
LA VANGUARDIA
- Average salary of worker on permanent contract is twice that of worker on temporary contract.
- Storms, snow and high winds which hit Cataluna worsened long weekend traffic.
- Democratic Union of Catalonia approved on Sunday reform in its political strategy which leaves door open for becoming Catalonia's principal political party.
- Barcelona football club signs Nigerian player Emmanuel Amunike after the team lost against Real Madrid on Saturday.
CINCO DIAS
- None of Spain's top 20 investment funds managing more than 150 bilion pesetas have succeeded in achieving an eight percent return this year.
- Telefonica chairman Juan Villalonga reorganises management plan of company.
EXPANSION
- Certain companies will agree three-year pact with Treasury which specifies how much they will pay from their profits.
- Food production companies criticise hypermarkets for selling products below their purchase price.
GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Liquidation of insurance companies has been carried out without control.
- Labour reform will be up and running from 1998 until 2010.
- Liberalisation of electricity sector and corresponding fall in tariffs will prompt electricity companies to cut their investments by 130 billion pesetas.
